clue.text: Politician raising chap with problem about hospital

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising something lifts it so it reads from the bottom up
to be about something is to surround it on every side

blocks.note: a chap is a man
H is the map and road-sign abbreviation for hospital
a rub is a difficulty, as in 'there's the rub'

explanation.surface: A politician hoists up a colleague who has a grievance about a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: The chap goes round the hospital, the problem follows, and in this down clue the whole string is then read upwards. Andy Burnham is the Labour Mayor of Greater Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: Andy Burnham is a British Labour figure and former cabinet minister, so he is an example of the category named.

clue.text: Plant set in patio awkwardly

indicators.note: something done awkwardly is done clumsily, so the letters come out in a jumble

blocks.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A gardener struggles to bed a plant into the paving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' and 'set' pull towards gardening verbs; the first word is the definition and the next three are simply the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The poinsettia is a Mexican shrub with red leafy bracts, popular as a Christmas houseplant.

clue.text: Part of brigade in capital

indicators.note: only a portion of the following word is wanted, a run of letters sitting inside it

blocks.note: letters two to five of the word

explanation.surface: A unit of soldiers is stationed in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of brigade' reads like a platoon or company; it is literally a run of letters inside the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Riga is the chief city and seat of government of Latvia, on the Baltic coast.

clue.text: Day with November gone to hide progress

indicators.note: something gone has been taken away, so one letter is dropped

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for day
to envelop something is to wrap it up out of sight
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A November day spent keeping progress out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: The wrapping verb loses its N, and D goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To develop is to grow or advance, a verb synonym of progress in its sense of moving forward.

clue.text: Last character following passion left detained by priest is director

indicators.note: someone detained is held inside, so these letters sit within others

blocks.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet
Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel, a crossword regular
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
fire is ardour or passion
standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: The final figure of a passion play left in a priest's custody turns out to be the director.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviations for following and left sit either side of the passion, all inside the priest. Franco Zeffirelli directed Romeo and Juliet and Jesus of Nazareth.
explanation.definitionFit: Franco Zeffirelli was an Italian film and opera director, so he is an example of the category named.

clue.text: Dishonest type in hide-out with switched contents

indicators.note: the inner letters swap places, so they run the other way round

blocks.note: an animal's or villain's den

explanation.surface: A crook lies low in a den where everything has been moved around.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the two middle letters of LAIR trade places; the L and R stay put.
explanation.definitionFit: A liar tells untruths, so a person who deceives is fairly called a dishonest type.

clue.text: One dubbed flipping guide missing opening farcical

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it so it runs the other way
without its opening, a word has lost its first letter

blocks.note: a knight is dubbed with a sword and becomes Sir
a bible is an authoritative guide, as in a cook's bible

explanation.surface: Someone calls a useless guide with its first page missing flipping ridiculous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British swear word; it is the reversal instruction. The guide loses its B.
explanation.definitionFit: Risible means laughable or ridiculous, a close synonym of farcical in the sense of absurd.

clue.text: Speak highly of one at a late stage in New York?

blocks.note: surface: someone well into old age, or a runner late in a race
setter's reading: 'late' means dead, praise of the dead is a funeral tribute, and New York wants the American spelling

explanation.walkthrough: The late are the dead, and speaking highly of them is what a funeral oration does. The question mark flags that New York is a spelling hint: Americans write -IZE where British setters often write -ISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To eulogize is to praise warmly, especially in a formal speech about someone who has died.

clue.text: Bring out client I fancy with no end of distinction

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter
having none of something means that letter is taken away
fancy as an adjective means elaborate or ornamental, so the letters get dressed up in a new order

blocks.note: the letters as printed
the last letter of the word, to be removed

explanation.surface: A lawyer admits a fancy for a client entirely lacking in distinction.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the N out of CLIENTI, then rearrange what is left. 'Fancy' reads as a verb after 'I'; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit is to draw a response or fact from someone, a verb synonym of draw out or evoke.

clue.text: Overwhelm sister among papers at rear of office

indicators.note: to be among things is to sit in their midst
the rear of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: identity papers
a nun is a religious sister
used as printed
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A sister is buried in paperwork at the back of the office.
explanation.walkthrough: The snowed-under office worker suits the answer; 'papers' is common crossword shorthand for ID, identification.
explanation.definitionFit: To inundate is to flood, and figuratively to swamp someone with more than they can handle.

clue.text: Refuse to allow car around British institute

indicators.note: going around something encloses it on both sides

blocks.note: a Ford is a make of car
standard abbreviation
standard abbreviation, as in MIT

explanation.surface: A British research body won't let cars be driven around its site.
explanation.walkthrough: The car maker's name goes around the two abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: To forbid is to prohibit or ban, which is exactly withholding permission.

clue.text: Quickly leave, like a woman fond of party footwear?

definitions.text: like a woman fond of party footwear?
definitions.note: a description of a person rather than a verb phrase

blocks.note: the idiom for running away

blocks.clueFragment: like a woman fond of party footwear?
blocks.note: to take to something is to grow fond of it, and heels are high-heeled shoes

explanation.surface: A partygoer rushes off, as a lover of stilettos would.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: take to (be fond of) plus your heels (shoes). The question mark flags the playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To take to your heels is an idiom for running off in a hurry, fleeing on foot.

clue.text: See Conservative in old country engaged in filming

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
a nation is a country
lo is an old word for look or see
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Spotting a Tory in some former nation while a film crew is at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like the verb to look at, but here it is the archaic interjection, as in 'lo and behold'.
explanation.definitionFit: Filming on location means shooting at a real site rather than in a studio.

clue.text: Imagined flying in nosedive

indicators.note: things sent flying are scattered, landing in a new order

blocks.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A pilot pictured the plane going into a nosedive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying' fits the aircraft picture so snugly that it is easy to miss as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To have envisioned something is to have pictured it in the mind, a synonym of imagined.

clue.text: Follow sound of wader

indicators.note: we want how a word is pronounced, not how it is written

blocks.note: a stork is a long-legged wading bird

explanation.surface: Tracking a wading bird by its call.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone works in standard British speech, where the R in the bird's name is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: To stalk someone is to follow or pursue them stealthily.

clue.text: Bit of garlic learner put in sheltered place

indicators.note: putting something in places it inside something else

blocks.note: L is for learner, from British learner-driver plates
a cove is a small sheltered bay

explanation.surface: A trainee cook stores some garlic somewhere out of the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit of' tempts you to take a single letter of garlic; the whole phrase is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A clove is one of the segments that make up a whole bulb of garlic.

clue.text: Stay in this way with diary having deleted a line

indicators.note: deleting removes letters, so part of the word is struck out

blocks.note: so means thus, in this way
a journal is a diary
A as printed plus L, the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A diarist records a visit, then crosses out a line.
explanation.walkthrough: The A and L come off the end of the diary word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sojourn is a temporary stay somewhere, and the word also works as a verb meaning to stay.

clue.text: A person in seat with Henry and Rita, maybe, has jar

blocks.note: used as printed
an MP holds a parliamentary seat
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
Rita Ora is a British pop singer; 'maybe' says she is one example of an Ora

explanation.surface: Someone seated beside Henry and Rita is holding a jar.
explanation.walkthrough: The names read as fellow guests at a table. Henry is the unit symbol H, and Rita points to the singer's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: An amphora is a tall two-handled vessel of ancient Greece and Rome, used for wine or oil.

clue.text: Note words of approval after leaving place on island

indicators.note: once something has left, it is no longer there

blocks.note: a compliment is a remark of praise
PL is the street-sign abbreviation for Place
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone murmurs praise as they leave a spot on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place on island' is PL placed on I, and those three letters come out of the middle of the praise word.
explanation.definitionFit: A note can be a brief remark or observation, just as a comment is.

clue.text: Claim noisy rooms disrupted major enquiry

indicators.note: something disrupted is thrown into disorder, so its letters get rearranged

blocks.note: the fifteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A complaint that loud rooms upset a big investigation.
explanation.walkthrough: The three opening words supply all fifteen letters. A Royal Commission is a formal public inquiry set up by the Crown in Britain and Commonwealth countries.
explanation.definitionFit: A Royal Commission is a high-level official investigation into a matter of public concern.

clue.text: Place to get round in sweltering island capital

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it

blocks.note: sweltering weather is hot
a bar is where you buy a round of drinks

explanation.surface: Where to buy a round of drinks in a hot island capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' tempts you towards the letter O, but it belongs to the pub phrase 'get a round in'; that 'in' also does the placing.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobart is the chief city of Tasmania, the island state of Australia.

clue.text: Family member frequented venue in Tower Hamlets?

indicators.note: this London East End borough is Cockney territory, where speakers drop the H sound

blocks.note: a haunt is a place you visit often

explanation.surface: A relative's regular local in East London.
explanation.walkthrough: Tower Hamlets is a borough in London's East End, home of Cockney speech, which drops an initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: An aunt is a parent's sister, so she is a relative within the family.

clue.text: Recall current religious teacher grabbing ordinary grilled fare

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the letters come back the other way
whatever grabs something holds it within

blocks.note: I is the symbol for electric current
a mullah is a Muslim cleric and teacher
O is ordinary, as in the old O level exam

explanation.surface: Remembering a teacher who reached for something plain off the grill.
explanation.walkthrough: MULLAH takes in O after its MU, I goes in front, and everything then runs backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Halloumi is a firm Cypriot cheese that holds its shape when grilled or fried.

clue.text: First off, observe feature of a canal

indicators.note: with the first taken off, a word starts one letter later

blocks.note: to clock is British slang for noticing

explanation.surface: An instruction to notice, first of all, something on a canal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First off' reads as 'to begin with'; it removes the opening letter of the slang verb for spotting something.
explanation.definitionFit: A lock is a gated chamber that raises or lowers boats between water levels on a canal.

clue.text: Pair almost in dominant position very quickly

indicators.note: almost all means nearly all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for pair
on top means in charge

explanation.surface: A pair nearly takes the lead at great speed.
explanation.walkthrough: ON TOP loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pronto is informal for immediately or at once, borrowed from Spanish for quick.

clue.text: Working in Greece shortly around clubs – what scouts have to do?

definitions.note: a description of the activity; the answer is a participle

indicators.note: working material is being shaped into something new
cut short, a word loses its last letter
going around something encloses it on both sides

blocks.note: used as printed
the country's name without its final letter
the card-suit abbreviation

explanation.surface: Scouts on a job in Greece, carrying their clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word placing the action in Greece, but it is part of the letters to rearrange. A recce is British informal for a reconnaissance, a scouting trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Military scouts reconnoitre ahead of a force, and recceing is the informal word for making that survey.
